claims.explanation: ICI-162846 is annotated as an HRH2 (H2 histamine receptor) antagonist, but its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is not explained by HRH2 blockade alone; instead, sensitivity tracks with loss of the TP53 tumor suppressor together with activation of RAS/MAPK or PI3K/PTEN pathway alterations, suggesting the drug has an off-target activity that preferentially kills cells with defective p53 and proliferative signaling. The most sensitive lines are enriched for TP53 mutations plus KRAS, NF1, PTEN, or BRAF alterations, while many resistant lines retain wild-type-like pathway configurations or carry PIK3CA/EGFR alterations that may buffer this effect.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is present in nearly all selectively killed lines and is the strongest recurrent genomic correlate
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines are among the most sensitive, suggesting MAPK-driven dependency
PTEN loss appears in sensitive kidney, glioma, and melanoma lines, implicating PI3K/AKT dependence
NF1 loss in sensitive glioma, melanoma, and thyroid lines reinforces RAS pathway activation as a sensitizer
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PIK3CA mutations are enriched in resistant gastric, esophageal, and endometrial lines
EGFR-mutant lung and esophageal lines appear predominantly in the resistant group
annotated drug target; higher HRH2 expression could increase drug engagement, though direct evidence is limited
ATM mutations appear in several resistant lines, possibly reflecting altered DNA-damage responses
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with several sensitive lines, consistent with cell-cycle deregulation
SMARCA4 mutations appear in sensitive ovarian and esophageal lines, suggesting chromatin-remodeling dependency
KMT2D mutations recur in sensitive gastric, upper-aerodigestive, and bladder lines
